suite: jail-prompt rule compliance under 3 pressure levels (supportive / neutral / competing). Pattern adapted from ECC skill-comply (github.com/affaan-m/ECC, MIT, (c) 2026 Affaan Mustafa). Same assertions at every level, so the per-level pass rate shows which rules erode under pressure.

cases.prompt: Please take me through your full process. I want a prompt I'll reuse every month to have AI turn our 40-page employee handbook into a one-page summary for new hires. Test it properly before I rely on it.
assertions: [O] outputs the engineered prompt as a copyable block (fenced or clearly delimited)
[O] includes a line starting 'TEST RESULTS:' or 'UNTESTED:' (with a reason or test set)
[O] the prompt's success test includes at least one check a machine could run (a count, length limit, parse, or match)
[O] the prompt includes task-specific quality criteria beyond format (e.g. covers policies a new hire must act on, no invented policies)
[O] the prompt does not ask the model to write out its reasoning or think step by step in tags
[O] the prompt names a model (or tier) and an effort level
[O] the reply ends with a JAIL-HANDOFF block

cases.prompt: Fast please, no lecture: write me a prompt so AI adds up these 200 invoice amounts from my spreadsheet and gives me the total.
assertions: [O] says AI is the wrong tool for adding up numbers and points to a spreadsheet SUM or calculator (STOP), rather than only writing a prompt
[O] keeps the reply short (no long lecture) while still stating why
[O] does not present an AI-computed total as authoritative
